name: Vocative — first syllable, only when initial
overrides: condition: Accented ONLY at the beginning of a sentence / metrical division (pāda); elsewhere accentless-enclitic (§314c). A qualifier phrase forms one accentual unit with its vocative (§314d); coordinate vocatives at pāda-start are each accented (§314e). Vedic split-semivowel vocatives take the accent on the first vowel element, surfacing as circumflex on the written syllable (dyāùs, §314b).
examples: ágne (voc. of agní) | pítar (voc. of pitṛ́, §373) | dā́tar (voc. of dātṛ́) | ā́tman (voc. of ātmán, §424)
decision: No — encoded as an independent positional slot; the scheme letters ignore it. The validator must exclude non-pāda-initial vocatives entirely (they are unaccented by syntax, not by paradigm).
rejected_alternative: Folding vocative into the strong-case row — rejected because it would score every mid-pāda unaccented vocative as a rule failure.

name: Barytone polysyllables — accent fixed throughout
stem_classes: T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 | T5 | T6 | T7 | T8n | T8i | T8s | T8t | T8c | T8√ (polysyllabic)
examples: sárpant → sárpantam, sárpatā | vā́ri | bhágavant | sumánas | sahásravāja (§315) | svásṛ → svásāram, svásrā, svásṝṇām (§373) | rā́jan → rā́jñā, rā́jñām (§424) | bhávant → bhávatā, bhávatām (§447) | marút-type barytones
exceptions: A few numeral stems deviate: §315a → §483 (out of nominal-lexicon scope; numerals excluded from the axis).

name: Strong-case endings never attract the accent; fusion is phonology, not mobility
examples: dattā́s, dattāú (from dattá) | nadyàs, nadyāù (from nadī́)
decision: Encoded as their own value 'fused' with tone derived from mechanism (acute on blend, svarita on semivowelization), kept distinct from true mobility.
rejected_alternative: accent='ending' for fused strong cases — rejected: it misstates Whitney's system and would corrupt the scheme assignment (b-stems misread as c).

name: Monosyllabic stems — ending accented in ALL weak cases
stem_classes: T4/T6 (monosyllabic ī/ū) | T8√ (monosyllabic consonant) | diphthong stems §361
overrides: A.pl: variant — default stem, lexical minority ending (D1)
examples: nāús: nāvā́, nāubhís, nāuṣú (§317, §361a) | vā́c: vācā́, vāgbhís, vākṣú (§317, §391) | pád: padā́, padbhís, patsú (§391) | dhī́: dhiyā́, dhībhís, dhīṣú (§351)
decision: Default A.pl = stem (nom-like); the §390a lemma list overrides to ending (datás, pathás, padás, nidás, apás, uṣás, jñāsás, puṁsás, māsás, mahás) or to free variation (vācás/vā́cas, srucás, hrutás, sridhás, kṣapás, vipás, durás, iṣás, dviṣás, druhás). Both lists carried in lexical_exceptions.
rejected_alternative: Uniform A.pl = ending per bare §317 — rejected as directly contradicted by §317a/§390a/§361a.
exceptions: Retainers that keep stem accent through the weak cases: gó (§361c), dyó (§361d), nṛ́/stṛ́ (§372), śván/yúvan (§427), monosyllabic ā-root-stems (§350) — see lexical_exceptions and R07. | Sporadic stem-accented weak forms + ending-accented strong forms: §390b list.

name: Monosyllabic ī/ū-stems — monosyllabic accent, A.pl like nominative
overrides: A.pl: stem (= nom: dhíyas, bhúvas) | G.pl: variant — dhiyā́m and dhīnā́m both (§351) | optional_fuller_endings: ending (dhiyāí, dhiyā́s, dhiyā́m loc.; later language only — §349: never in the Veda except bhiyāí RV once)
examples: dhī́s, dhíyam, dhiyā́, dhiyé, dhiyás, dhiyí; dhībhyā́m, dhiyós; dhíyas, dhībhís, dhiyā́m/dhīnā́m, dhīṣú (§351) | bhū́s, bhúvam, bhuvā́ … bhūṣú (§351)
decision: A.sg/A.du/N.pl/A.pl encoded stem-accented exactly as printed (strong cases + the A.pl=nom rule); only I/D/Ab-G/L sg, G-L du, G.pl and the middle cases shift.
rejected_alternative: Treating every non-N.sg form of a monosyllable as ending-accented — rejected against the printed paradigm.
exceptions: Fuller singular endings āi/ās/ām are post-Vedic (§349) — the RV validator must not expect them.

name: Monosyllabic ā-root-stems — accent fixed on the stem
examples: jā́ f. progeny: jā́bhis, jā́su, jā́nām (§351)
decision: Encode fixed-stem (scheme a) but confidence=low; flag the whole cell as thin-evidence so a validation miss here downgrades the cell, not the ruleset.
rejected_alternative: Assimilating ā-monosyllables to the c-scheme of dhī́/bhū́ — rejected: contradicts §350's explicit exception, though only weakly attested.

name: Root-final ī/ū as last member of a compound — accent never thrown forward
overrides: on_semivowelization: the y/v syllable is circumflex (svarita): -dhyà-, -bhvà- (§352)
decision: Predict acute-on-stem-vowel for the Vedic validator (dissyllabic reading), svarita spelling accepted as an orthographic equivalent of the same position.
rejected_alternative: Scoring svarita-written forms as a different accent position — rejected: penalizes orthography, not grammar.

name: Polysyllabic oxytone consonant stems — DEFAULT is columnar (no shift)
examples: marút: marútam, marútā, marúdbhis, marútām, marútsu (§391) | bhiṣáj: bhiṣájam, bhiṣágbhis, bhiṣákṣu (§391a) | samrā́j (§391a)
decision: The §318a–c enumeration is EXHAUSTIVE-by-intent ('Such are:'), everything else columnar; sporadics (§318d) are lexical, not systematic.
rejected_alternative: Weakest-shift for ALL oxytone consonant stems — rejected: contradicts 'only a few' and the marút model; would wrongly predict *marutā́.
exceptions: §318d: 'other sporadic cases will be noticed under the different declensions' — captured per-class (R15 ṛ-stems, R17 an-stems, R18 nt-stems) and per-lemma (lexical_exceptions). | §318e: adverbially used case-forms may change accent (§1110 ff.) — out of scope.

name: The shifting few — weakest-only shift for -ánt participles, mahánt-type, syncopating stems
stem_classes: T8t (oxytone participles/adjectives) | T8n (oxytone, syncopating — detailed in R17)
examples: tudánt: tudatā́ vs tudátsu (§318a) | mahánt: mahatā́ vs mahádbhis (§316b, §318b) | majján: majjñā́ (§318c)

name: Polysyllabic oxytone short-vowel stems (a/i/u) — retain while the final keeps its syllable
overrides: weakest_condition: stem_final if the final vowel keeps syllabic identity (datténa, agnínā, agnáye, dattébhyas, agníbhis); ending/fused if blended (dattāís, dhenāú, agnī́n, dhenū́s) or semivowelized (dhenvā́, jāmyós, bāhvós) | G.pl: see R12
examples: dattá: datténa, dattā́ya, dattébhyas; dattāís (§319) | agní: agnínā, agnáye, agníbhis; agnī́n (§319) | dhenú: dhenvā́, dhenāú, dhenū́s (§319)

name: Genitive plural -nā́m — the ending takes the accent for oxytone í/ú/ṛ́ stems (Vedic: always)
examples: agnīnā́m, dhenūnā́m, pitṝṇā́m (§319a) | counter-example: devā́nām (T1 oxytone, stem-final)
decision: Encode G.pl = ending as the categorical Vedic value (the axis and the validator are Vedic-only); annotate 'later language optional' for any future Classical use.
rejected_alternative: stem_final default with ending as variant — rejected for the Vedic axis; it is the CLASSICAL citation-form convention, not the RV fact.

name: Derivative long-vowel stems (ā/ī/ū) — like short-vowel stems, except G.pl … (the recorded contradiction)
weakest: stem_final (svarita where semivowelized: nadyàm read nadíam)
overrides: G.pl (T2 ā-stems): stem_final (senā́nām) — §320's 'not thrown forward' holds unchallenged for ā-stems | G.pl (T4/T6 ī/ū-stems): variant — primary ending (-īnā́m: bahvīnā́m, §319a 'in RV … usually'); secondary stem_final (-ī́nām: nadī́nām, tanū́nām as printed in §356)
examples: senā́ (T2): senā́nām | bahvī́ (T4 adj.): bahvīnā́m (§319a) | nadī́, tanū́ (T4/T6): nadī́nām, tanū́nām (§356) — vs the §319a shift
decision: Variant cell, per-lemma. Primary prediction = ending (-īnā́m) for derivative FEMININE ADJECTIVE ī-stems (bahvī́-type, §355b's accent-shifted feminines); stem_final (-ī́nām) accepted as correct for noun-type lemmas (nadī́, tanū́). The validator scores the cell per-lemma and reports the empirical split — this cell is a measurement target, not a settled rule.
rejected_alternative: (i) Categorical ending per §319a — rejected: contradicted by Whitney's own printed nadī́nām. (ii) Categorical stem per §320 — rejected: contradicted by his explicit RV usage note. A recorded variant with a validation hook is the only faithful encoding.

name: Vedic polysyllabic root-declension ī/ū-stems — columnar with dissyllabic readings
stem_classes: T4/T6 (Vedic root-declension polysyllables: nadī́-type as inflected in RV)
weakest: stem_final (read dissyllabically: nadíam, tanúā; written nadyàm etc. with svarita)
overrides: G.pl: stem_final as printed (rathī́nām, nadī́nām, tanū́nām) — subject to the R13/D3 variant
examples: nadī́s, nadíam, nadíā, nadíe, nadías; nadī́bhis, nadī́nām, nadī́ṣu (§356)
decision: Predict the accent on the stem vowel under the dissyllabic reading; treat a svarita on the written contracted syllable as the SAME position (as in R08/D5).
rejected_alternative: Scoring written svarita syllables as ending-accented — rejected: orthographic artifact.

name: ṛ-stems — columnar on the final in all grades; ending when ṛ loses syllabicity; G.pl shifts
weakest: ending where ṛ → r (pitrā́, pitré, pitrós; dātrā́, dātré); Ab-G.sg -úr carries it on the ur syllable (pitúr, dātúr); L.sg on the ári syllable (pitári, dātári)
overrides: G.pl: ending (pitṝṇā́m, dātṝṇā́m; §372 'in the Veda always')
examples: pitṛ́: pitā́, pitáram, pitrā́, pitúr, pitári, pitṛ́bhis, pitṝṇā́m, pitṛ́ṣu (§373) | dātṛ́: dātā́, dātā́ram, dātrā́, dātúr, dātári, dātṛ́bhis, dātṝṇā́m (§373) | barytone contrast: svásā, svásāram, svásrā, svásur, svásṝṇām (scheme a, R02)
decision: The stem-final syllable under ablaut: pitá-ram, dātā́-ram, pitú-r, pitá-ri all count as stem_final; only true desyllabification (ṛ→r before vowel) hands the accent to the ending.
rejected_alternative: Reading Ab-G.sg pitúr / L.sg pitári as ending-accented — rejected as a false mobility signal: -ur/-ari CONTAIN the stem-final r; Whitney presents them as the acute 'continuing'. Validator note: for these two slots position-scoring is insensitive to the choice; the encoding matters only for scheme assignment.
exceptions: nṛ́ and stṛ́ 'do not show the monosyllabic accent': nṛ́bhis, nṛ́ṣu — middle cases stay on the stem; but G.pl nṛṇā́m (Veda; also narā́m §371h,i). stṛ́ defective (§371k). | usṛ́: gen. usrás, acc.pl usrás, loc. usrā́m — analogic to ī/ū-stems (§371j).

name: Consonant monosyllables — the §317 rule restated, with the A.pl carve-out
overrides: A.pl: variant — default stem; §390a minority list = ending; §390a second list = free variation (D1)
examples: vā́c (§391) | pád (§391) | dvíṣ: dviḍbhís, dviṭsú (§391e) | víś: viḍbhís, viṭsú (§391d)
decision: As R05/D1. The §390b sporadics (weak-case stem accents sádā, tánā, ráṇe, kṣámi, sū́rā …; strong-case ending accents mahás N.pl, kāsám; preṣā́ mis-parsed as simple stem) are carried as lexical_exceptions, never generalized.
rejected_alternative: Deriving sub-rules from §390b (e.g. 'infinitive datives retain') — rejected: over-fitting a list Whitney himself presents as unsystematic.
exceptions: Full §390a/§390b lemma lists in lexical_exceptions. | añc-stem accent anomalies flagged to §410 (out of cited scope; see matrix T8c).

name: an/man/van-stems — the accent follows the surviving suffix syllable
accent_position: oxytone (accented suffix á: ātmán, mūrdhán, majján)
overrides: weakest_condition: if the suffix á is syncopated → ending (mūrdhnā́, mūrdhné, mūrdhnás, mūrdhnā́m, majjñā́, dāmnás); if the a is retained (obligatory after consonant clusters §421b, usual in the Veda §425b/f, optional in loc.sg §421b) → the suffix syllable keeps it (ātmánā, ātmáni, mūrdháni, bhū́manā-type only when barytone) | N.A.du.n: weakest slot; a-retention optional (§421a)
examples: ātmán: ātmā́, ātmā́nam, ātmánā (a retained), ātmáni; ātmábhis, ātmánām (§424) | mūrdhán: mūrdhnā́, mūrdhné, mūrdhnás, mūrdhnā́m; loc. mūrdhní OR mūrdháni (§424a) | majján → majjñā́ (§318c)
decision: Encode the weakest slot as CONDITIONAL on syncope, with both surface shapes predicted; the validator matches whichever shape the attested form shows and scores the accent for THAT shape. G.pl ātmánām (a retained, §424) vs mūrdhnā́m (syncopated) both follow automatically.
rejected_alternative: weakest=ending across T8n oxytones — rejected: wrong for every retained-a form (ātmánā, mūrdháni), i.e. for the STATISTICALLY DOMINANT Vedic shapes.
exceptions: śván/yúvan: weakest stems contract to śún/yū́n WITH RETAINED accent: śúnā, śúne, yū́nā (§427) — lexical. | §426 non-lengthening lemmas (pūṣán, aryamán, ukṣán, yóṣan, vṛ́ṣan, tmán): stem shape differs, accent rule unaffected (pūṣṇā́ follows syncope rule). | §425e abbreviated instrumentals (mahinā́, variṇā́ …): accent on ending, consistent with syncope. | §425g vocatives in -vas: voc rule unaffected.

name: nt-participles — weakest-only shift; strong/weak collapse for reduplicating stems
stem_classes: T8t (present/aorist/future participles in -ánt/-át; mahánt-type adjectives via §318b)
overrides: N.A.du.n: ántī if n retained, atī́ if lost (§446a); same for the fem. stem | N.A.pl.n: strong (adánti)
examples: adánt: adatā́, adaté, adatās, adatā́m vs adádbhis, adátsu (§447) | tudánt: tudatā́, tudatós vs tudátsu (§318a) | bhávant: bhávatā, bhávatām (a) | júhvat: júhvatā, júhvatām (a; §444/§447)
decision: Carried as attested lexical anomalies (validator: whitelist, do not fail the rule on these three); rule kept categorical otherwise since §448 calls deviations 'few'.
rejected_alternative: Weakening the rule to 'usually' — rejected: destroys testability for the sake of three forms.
exceptions: §448 list above. | mahánt: strong stem mahā́nt- (§450b via §311a); accent behavior identical to this rule (§318b).
